html:
The Lule were a people of the dry forests and plains of northwest Argentina, in today's Salta, Tucumán and Santiago del Estero. Spanish records of the 1500s and 1600s describe them as hunters, fishers and gatherers, often at war with the farming Diaguita and Tonocoté peoples of the region.

The Spanish founded towns such as Tucumán and Salta on or near their land. In the 1700s Jesuit missionaries gathered many Lule into missions on the Salado River, and the Jesuit Antonio Machoni published a grammar of their language in 1732. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, the missions declined and the Lule merged into the mixed rural population of Argentina. See also Jesuit missions.
